land.text: Tripoli and its surroundings, from which Burghul expelled 'Ali ibn Mehmed Karamanli on 30 July 1793

predecessors.note: The page lists the belligerent as 'Ottoman Tripolitania (1793-1795)'; Panzac calls Burghul 'an Algerian usurper who claimed to be supported by the sultan', Abun-Nasr says he 'secured the Ottoman government's approval for his invasion of Tripolitania'.

land.text: Tripoli, regained by Hamet and Yusuf Karamanli on 19 January 1795

successors.note: Hamet ruled from 20 January to 11 June 1795, when Yusuf deposed him.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: Burghul held Tripoli from 30 July 1793 until the Karamanli returned on 19 January 1795.

rulers.title: usurper, Ottoman-backed
rulers.note: Entered Tripolitania on 29 July 1793 and fled to Egypt after 19 January 1795.

correction.text: Tripoli and its surroundings, held from 30 July 1793 to 19 January 1795

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, state Cliopatria lacks (it draws the Karamanli over these years). The page says Burghul 'expelled Ali ibn Mehmed Karamanli' and ruled Tripolitania in the name of the sultan, but gives no extent beyond Tripoli; the Karamanli held out elsewhere (Yusuf in revolt) and the radius of 80 km is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Tripoli, the seat of the Karamanli

ledger.note: 29-30 July 1793: Ali Burghul seizes Tripoli. He entered Tripolitania with nine merchant ships and about 300 mercenaries on 29 July 1793 and expelled 'Ali ibn Mehmed Karamanli on 30 July; Ali fled to Tunis.
30 July 1793: Tripoli passes from the Karamanli to Burghul, who would 'rule it in the name of the sultan' (Abun-Nasr).

region.text: Djerba, the island occupied by Burghul

ledger.note: 30 September 1794: Burghul occupies Djerba, an island under Hammuda ibn Ali, the Bey of Tunis, who had hesitated to act against Burghul because Burghul claimed the sultan's authority, and acted after the occupation.
19 January 1795: Burghul's hold on Djerba ends with his flight. The page does not say what became of Djerba after the occupation of 30 September 1794; the Tunis dossier lists no Djerba event.
19 January 1795: Hamet and Yusuf return to Tripoli 'with the aid of the Bey of Tunis and the rebels' and Burghul flees to Egypt.

January 1795: the Burghul regime ends. Ali ibn Mehmed renounced the governorship in favour of Hamet, who ruled as Ahmad II Pasha from 20 January; the infobox ends the war on 20 January 1795 with a 'Karamanli victory'.

wars.name: Tripolitanian civil war

zones.text: Tripoli, held by Burghul from 30 July 1793 to 19 January 1795

wars.outcome: Karamanli victory: the Karamanli return to Tripoli on 19 January 1795 with the aid of the Bey of Tunis and the rebels; Burghul flees to Egypt.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war July 1790 - 20 January 1795; the page gives Yusuf's rebellion as June 1791 in one place and June 1793 in another.

certainty.note: A city and its hinterland held for eighteen months; no frontier is on the page.

sources.title: Tripolitanian civil war
sources.note: The only page opened for this dossier: Burghul's coup, Djerba, the return of the Karamanli. It is also the karamanli-dynasty dossier's source for 1793-1795.

notes: Ali Burghul (af-02-f): a usurper regime that held Tripoli for eighteen months (30 July 1793 - 19 January 1795), written as type rebel because rule 5 (loss and gain against a rebel-type counterpart) is the way to draw it; the Karamanli dossier carries the matching loss and gain. Cliopatria has no row for it. The extent beyond Tripoli (80 km) is the researcher's reading; the page names nothing else. The Karamanli page dates the Karamanli return January 1794, this page 19 January 1795. Djerba is not in the gazetteer (coordinates 10.85 E, 33.8 N used); the Tunis dossier records no Djerba event, so the contest pair here has no mirror there. Wikipedia title given is the civil-war article; there is no article on Burghul's regime.
